$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

The triple integral above is defined over the type III region given by

$$
S={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2x,\,0\le y\le xz}.
$$

For a fixed admissible $x$, let $[a(x),b(x)]$ be the full nonempty $z$ fiber of the exactly specified region $S$. What is $a(x)+b(x)$?
authoring.rationale: Preserve S and key2x; actual x projection[0,2] excludes negative x where z bounds reverse.

authoring.question: q-161712
authoring.value:
The defining set $S$ is retained exactly. The requirement $0\le z\le2x$ has no solution for $x<0$, so the actual outer range is $0\le x\le2$. For each such $x$, the full $z$ interval is $[0,2x]$, and $xz\ge0$ makes the $y$ interval $[0,xz]$ nonempty. Hence

$$a(x)+b(x)=0+2x=2x,\qquad \iiint_S f\,dV=\int_0^2\int_0^{2x}\int_0^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.$$

For $f=1$, the true volume is $\int_0^2 2x^3\,dx=8$. The source solution retained the nominal outer range $[-1,2]$ and included reversed $z$ bounds on negative $x$, giving the signed value $15/2$. That outer-bound error does not change the requested middle-endpoint sum $2x$.
authoring.rationale: Preserve S and key2x; actual x projection[0,2] excludes negative x where z bounds reverse.
